title: AmbientCore — User Handbook
content_md:
# AmbientCore — User Handbook

Welcome to **AmbientCore**, your AI-operated company platform. This handbook covers everything you need to navigate the system, understand the agents, and work with the dashboard.

---

## What Is AmbientCore?

AmbientCore is an autonomous operating system where AI agents handle day-to-day operations across every department. You — the CEO — retain full authority, with agents executing within governed boundaries.

The system runs on a **heartbeat cycle** — every 30 minutes, agents wake up, assess the workspace, execute tasks, and report back. Between heartbeats, you can review work, approve actions, and steer priorities.

---

## Dashboard Overview

The sidebar on the left is your main navigation. Here's what each page does:

### Operations
- **Dashboard** — Live metrics: agent activity, token usage, session logs, heartbeat status
- **Standup** — Structured decision engine. Trigger standups to get agent recommendations on open tasks
- **Meetings** — Schedule and review team meetings with agents
- **Costs** — Financial overview, budget tracking, API costs, resource usage
- **Social Analytics** — Cross-platform metrics for X, LinkedIn, and Bluesky
- **Memory Stack** — Agent memory layers (L1-L6) visualization

### Work
- **Overview** — Task board snapshot, action queue, wiki status
- **Tasks** — Kanban-style task board. Every agent generates and claims tasks. Filter by agent, status, goal, or campaign
- **Actions** — Command center for external actions (social posts, document publishing). All actions require your approval
- **Wiki** — Internal knowledge base: specs, runbooks, release notes, and governance docs

### Strategy
- **Overview** — Projects, goals, governance snapshot
- **Goals** — Objectives with measurable progress tracking
- **Campaigns** — Projects and directives. CEO creates, Nova translates, agents execute
- **Calendar** — Important dates, milestones, deadlines
- **Playbook** — Full governance documentation

### Content
- **Image Engine** — AI image generation pipeline
- **Gallery** — Published content library and generated assets

### Config
- **Overview** — System health, API status, agent configs
- **Automation** — Worker automation and agent automation settings
- **Workspace** — Company identity, mission, brand voice, tools, CEO notes
- **Memory** — CEO-curated seed memories that shape how agents think

---

## Getting Started

1. **Start with the Dashboard** — Get a feel for agent activity and system health
2. **Check Tasks daily** — See what agents are working on
3. **Review the Approval Queue** — Actions wait for your approval before executing
4. **Use Goals to steer** — Agents prioritize tasks that align with active goals
5. **Seed Agent Memory** — Shape how agents behave by writing seed memories in the Workspace

title: Meet Your Agents
content_md:
# Meet Your Agents

Your workspace comes with a team of 8 AI agents. Each one has a specific role, a department to run, and a personality that shapes how they approach problems. Think of them as your always-on executive team — they work every heartbeat cycle (every 30 minutes), read the current state of the workspace, and take action within their authority.

You, the CEO, sit at **Tier 1**. You have final say on everything. The agents operate below you in a clear hierarchy.

---

## The Hierarchy

```
Tier 1 — CEO (You)
  └─ Tier 2 — Nova (Prime Operator)
       ├─ Tier 3 — Cipher (CFO)
       ├─ Tier 3 — Pixel (Design & QC)
       ├─ Tier 3 — Forge (DevOps)
       ├─ Tier 3 — Echo (Marketing)
       ├─ Tier 3 — Scribe (Content)
       │    └─ Tier 4 — Quill (Editor)
       └─ Tier 3 — Scout (Research)
```

---

## Nova — Prime Operator (Tier 2)

Nova is your right hand. She translates your high-level goals and projects into concrete execution plans, then delegates work to the department heads. Every morning she runs the Daily Standup and surfaces what matters.

**What Nova does:**
- Breaks your projects down into tasks and assigns them to the right agent
- Runs the daily standup — summarizes progress, flags blockers, proposes next steps
- Monitors execution across all departments
- Escalates anything risky or cross-functional to you
- Receives worker intelligence reports and acts on findings

**Nova's core question:** *"Does this increase our leverage?"*

---

## Cipher — CFO (Tier 3)

**Department:** Finance & Operations

Cipher keeps the books. He tracks API costs, monitors budgets, and flags anything that looks like waste. If spending spikes, Cipher will notice before you do.

**What Cipher does:**
- Tracks API usage costs (Gemini, Azure, third-party services)
- Produces weekly cost reports every Monday
- Analyzes ROI on campaigns and content
- Flags budget drift or unexpected cost spikes
- Recommends resource optimizations

**Cipher's core question:** *"What is the ROI and downside risk?"*

---

## Pixel — Design & QC Lead (Tier 3)

**Department:** Frontend & Quality Assurance

Pixel owns the look and feel. She audits the UI for consistency, checks accessibility, and makes sure design standards are maintained across every page.

**What Pixel does:**
- Reviews UI changes for visual consistency
- Runs accessibility audits every Wednesday
- Checks color contrast, responsive layouts, and component patterns
- Flags design regressions or inconsistencies
- Maintains the design system and visual standards

**Pixel's core question:** *"Is this intentional design?"*

---

## Forge — DevOps Lead (Tier 3)

**Department:** Backend, Security & Infrastructure

Forge keeps the lights on. He monitors deployments, watches uptime, and makes sure nothing breaks at scale. If a build fails or a service goes down, Forge is the first to respond.

**What Forge does:**
- Monitors deployments and build status every 30 minutes
- Pings uptime checks every 15 minutes
- Audits infrastructure for security and performance
- Reviews CI/CD pipelines and deployment health
- Flags stability risks before they become outages

**Forge's core question:** *"Will this break at scale?"*

---

## Echo — Marketing Lead (Tier 3)

**Department:** Content Creative & Community

Echo is the voice of the brand. She drafts social posts, plans campaigns, and keeps content flowing across X, LinkedIn, and Bluesky. She makes sure you stay visible.

**What Echo does:**
- Drafts social media posts for all platforms
- Plans and executes marketing campaigns
- Maintains brand voice and messaging consistency
- Produces weekly social drafts every Tuesday
- Tracks engagement and adjusts content strategy

**Echo's core question:** *"Are we visible?"*

---

## Scribe — Content Lead (Tier 3)

**Department:** Content Creation & Publishing Pipeline

Scribe handles the long-form work — documentation, product briefs, blog posts, and wiki pages. Everything that needs to be written well goes through Scribe. He manages Quill (the editor) and owns the publishing pipeline.

**What Scribe does:**
- Writes long-form documentation and product briefs
- Creates and updates wiki pages (specs, runbooks, release notes)
- Manages the content-to-publish pipeline
- Ensures all published content meets quality standards
- Routes drafts through editing (Quill) before submission

**Scribe's core question:** *"Is this unambiguous?"*

---

## Scout — Research & Intelligence (Tier 3)

**Department:** Market Intelligence & Strategic Research

Scout watches the landscape. She uses live web search to track competitors, spot market trends, and find strategic opportunities before anyone else.

**What Scout does:**
- Conducts market research and competitive analysis
- Monitors industry trends and platform changes
- Identifies growth opportunities and strategic risks
- Benchmarks against competitors
- Delivers research briefs to inform strategy

**Scout's core question:** *"Where is leverage hiding?"*

---

## Quill — Content Editor (Tier 4)

**Reports to:** Scribe

Quill is the detail person. He polishes everything Scribe produces — tightening copy, enforcing brand voice, and compressing content until every word earns its place. Quill can't publish or create tasks directly; everything routes through Scribe.

**What Quill does:**
- Copy-edits all long-form content
- Enforces brand voice and tone consistency
- Compresses and clarifies writing
- Polishes calls-to-action
- Catches redundancy and vague language

**Quill's core question:** *"Can this be 20% clearer?"*

---

## How Agents Communicate

Agents don't chat with each other in real time. Instead, they share context through the **workspace state** — tasks, comments, documents, and memory. During each heartbeat cycle, every agent reads the latest state and decides what to do next.

If you want to talk to an agent directly, use **Quick Chat** (the floating button in the lower-right corner of any page). You can pick any agent from the dropdown and ask them questions, give instructions, or get their perspective.

---

## How Agents Learn

Agents carry a 6-layer memory stack into every heartbeat:

| Layer | Name | What It Contains |
|-------|------|------------------|
| L1 | Personality | The agent's core identity and role definition |
| L2 | Doctrine | Strategic bias, risk tolerance, escalation triggers |
| L3 | Seed Memories | CEO-curated memories (you write these in Config > Memory) |
| L4 | Runtime Memory | Dynamic memories accumulated during operation |
| L5 | CEO Notes | Your workspace notes, visible to all agents |
| L6 | Site Digest | Static site intelligence extracted from the codebase |

You can directly influence agent behavior by writing **seed memories** (L3) and **CEO notes** (L5). These are injected into every agent's prompt at every heartbeat.

---

## Quick Reference

| Agent | Role | Tier | Color | Key Automation |
|-------|------|------|-------|----------------|
| Nova | Prime Operator | 2 | Purple | Daily Standup (9 AM) |
| Cipher | CFO | 3 | Green | Weekly Cost Report (Mon 8 AM) |
| Pixel | Design & QC | 3 | Pink | Accessibility Scan (Wed 10 AM) |
| Forge | DevOps | 3 | Orange | Deploy Monitor (every 30 min) |
| Echo | Marketing | 3 | Cyan | Weekly Social Draft (Tue 10 AM) |
| Scribe | Content | 3 | Teal | On-demand |
| Scout | Research | 3 | Magenta | On-demand |
| Quill | Editor | 4 | Dark Teal | On-demand |

title: Automation & Controls
content_md:
# Automation & Controls

This guide explains how the automated systems work behind the scenes — the heartbeat, workers, agent automations, and the controls you have to dial autonomy up or down.

---

## The Heartbeat

The heartbeat is the engine that drives everything. It runs **every 30 minutes**, automatically.

Here's what happens each cycle:

1. **Lock acquired** — The system grabs a concurrency lock so two heartbeats can't run at the same time
2. **Context loaded** — Reads the full workspace state: tasks, documents, goals, campaigns, memories, agent configs
3. **Worker analysis** — Background workers check for pressure spikes and produce intelligence reports
4. **Agent execution** — Each agent reads the current state, evaluates their domain, and proposes or executes actions
5. **Task mutations** — New tasks created, existing tasks updated or moved between lanes
6. **Document actions** — Wiki pages created or updated, social drafts queued
7. **Governance check** — Every action is validated against authority rules and execution mode
8. **Reporting** — Results logged to the session log, governance log, and audit trail
9. **Lock released** — Heartbeat completes, system waits for the next cycle

You can also **trigger a heartbeat manually** from the Dashboard at any time using the "Run Heartbeat" button.

---

## Workers

Workers are **background analyzers** that activate during pressure spikes — when there's a backlog of tasks, a queue of pending reviews, or unusual activity patterns.

Key things to understand about workers:

- **They are read-only.** Workers analyze the workspace and produce reports, but they don't change anything directly.
- **They recommend actions.** Worker reports contain proposed actions that Nova reviews and decides whether to act on.
- **Only Nova sees worker reports.** Worker intelligence is injected into Nova's context during heartbeat, and she decides how to respond.
- **They activate automatically.** You don't need to trigger workers — they spin up when the system detects elevated workload.

You can see worker status and recent reports in **OPS > Overview** under the Worker Automation section.

---

## Agent Automations

Each agent has scheduled automations — recurring tasks they run on a fixed schedule:

| Agent | Automation | Schedule |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| Nova | Daily Standup Summary | Every day at 9:00 AM |
| Cipher | Weekly Cost Report | Every Monday at 8:00 AM |
| Pixel | Accessibility Scan | Every Wednesday at 10:00 AM |
| Forge | Deploy Monitor | Every 30 minutes |
| Forge | Uptime Ping | Every 15 minutes |
| Echo | Weekly Social Draft | Every Tuesday at 10:00 AM |

Scribe, Scout, and Quill work **on-demand** — they activate during heartbeat cycles when there's relevant work in their domain.

You can view and manage agent automations in **Config > Automation**.

---

## Execution Modes

Execution mode is your master dial for how much autonomy agents have. There are three settings:

### Live Mode
Full automation. Agents create tasks, move work between lanes, produce documents, and execute actions within their authority. This is the default.

**Use when:** Everything is running normally and you trust the current workflow.

### Safe Mode
Read-only for task mutations. Agents can still produce documents and add comments, but they **cannot** create, update, or move tasks. Think of it as observation mode — agents see everything but can't change the board.

**Use when:** You want to observe agent behavior without letting them change task state, or you're making manual adjustments and don't want interference.

### Locked Mode
Complete shutdown. No mutations of any kind — no tasks, no documents, no comments. The heartbeat still runs but exits immediately without doing anything.

**Use when:** You need a full stop. Maybe you're doing maintenance, or you want to freeze the workspace while you make strategic decisions.

Only the CEO can change execution mode. Find the toggle in **Config > Automation** or on the **Dashboard**.

---

## Project Freeze

Beyond the global execution mode, you can freeze individual projects:

- **Pause a project** — All tasks under that project are immediately frozen. No agent can create, update, or move tasks linked to the paused project.
- **Resume a project** — Tasks unfreeze and agents can work on them again in the next heartbeat.

This is useful when you want to keep most of the system running but temporarily halt work on a specific initiative.

Project freeze is **subordinate** to execution mode — if the system is in Locked mode, pausing or resuming a project has no effect until you switch back to Live or Safe.

---

## Approval Queue

Not everything runs on autopilot. The approval queue is where actions land when they need your sign-off.

Actions are auto-classified based on risk:

| Classification | Risk Level | What Happens |
|---------------|------------|---------------|
| **Autonomous** | Low risk, low budget, low brand impact | Executes automatically — no approval needed |
| **Advisory** | Medium risk or brand impact | Goes to your approval queue |
| **Executive Required** | High risk, high brand impact, or budget > $100 | Must be approved before anything happens |

In the approval queue, you can:
- **Approve** — Action executes immediately
- **Reject** — Action is cancelled with a reason logged
- **Request Revision** — Sent back to the originating agent for changes
- **Override** — Force-execute with a logged override event

Every approval decision is recorded in the **Governance Log** for full audit trail.

---

## Governance Rules

When an agent wants to do something, the system checks a priority stack to decide if it's allowed:

1. **Governance Rules** — Tier hierarchy, approval gates, security guardrails (highest priority)
2. **CEO Authority** — Your veto, overrides, and directives
3. **Budget Constraints** — CFO thresholds, API limits, resource caps
4. **Infrastructure Constraints** — Uptime, security, deployment stability
5. **Agent Doctrine** — Each agent's strategic bias (40% weight on decisions)
6. **Agent Preference** — Individual initiative and task prioritization (lowest priority)

This means governance rules always win. An agent can't override budget constraints just because their doctrine says to move fast. And your authority always trumps agent preferences.

---

## Tips

- **Start in Live mode** and switch to Safe if you want to observe without interference
- **Check the Dashboard regularly** — it shows the current execution mode, last heartbeat time, and approval queue count
- **Use project freeze** instead of global mode changes when you only need to pause one initiative
- **Review the Governance Log** periodically — it shows every approval, rejection, and override for full transparency
- **Worker reports are informational** — if you see worker findings in OPS > Overview, Nova is already aware and factoring them into her decisions

title: Typical Workflow — Your Daily Routine
content_md:
# Typical Workflow — Your Daily Routine

This guide walks through what a normal day looks like as CEO. You don't need to be here 24/7 — agents work autonomously between your check-ins. But a few minutes of attention each day keeps the whole machine aligned.

---

## Morning Check-In (5-10 minutes)

### 1. Open the Dashboard

Start at **OPS > Dashboard**. This is your control room. At a glance you can see:

- **Last heartbeat** — When agents last ran and what they did
- **Approval queue count** — How many items need your attention
- **Agent activity** — Who's been active and what they've touched
- **Token usage & costs** — How much AI compute is being used
- **System health** — Any errors or warnings

If the approval queue has items, handle those first.

### 2. Clear the Approval Queue

Go to **WORK > Actions** and check the queue. Each item shows:

- What action is proposed (social post, document publish, task change)
- Which agent proposed it and why
- Risk classification and Nova's recommendation

For each item, you can **Approve**, **Reject**, or **Request Revision**. Most low-risk items are already handled automatically — what lands in your queue genuinely needs your judgment.

### 3. Check the Standup

Head to **OPS > Standup**. Nova summarizes what happened overnight:

- Tasks completed, moved, or blocked
- New proposals from agents
- Progress on active goals and campaigns
- Any escalations or flags

This is your briefing. If something needs attention, you'll see it here.

---

## Steering Work (as needed)

### Set Goals

Go to **PLAN > Goals** to create or update objectives. Goals are what agents optimize toward — when you create a goal, agents will start generating tasks and proposals that move the needle.

Each goal has:
- A title and description
- Measurable targets
- Progress tracking (auto-updated as tasks complete)

### Create Campaigns

Campaigns are larger initiatives — think product launches, marketing pushes, or infrastructure upgrades. Create them at **PLAN > Campaigns**.

When you create a campaign:
1. Nova breaks it down into executable tasks
2. Tasks get assigned to the right department heads
3. Agents start working on their portion during the next heartbeat
4. Progress tracks automatically as tasks move through the board

### Manage Tasks Directly

If you want to get hands-on, go to **WORK > Tasks**. The Kanban board shows everything:

- **Backlog** — Work that hasn't started
- **In Progress** — Actively being worked on
- **Review** — Completed but needs verification
- **Done** — Finished and verified

You can create tasks manually, reassign them, add comments, or move them between lanes. Agents will see your changes at the next heartbeat and adjust accordingly.

---

## Content & Communications

### Review Social Drafts

Echo drafts social posts for X, LinkedIn, and Bluesky. Check **WORK > Actions** for queued social posts. Each draft includes:

- The post text
- Target platform
- Attached URL (required for all social posts)
- Echo's reasoning for the post

Approve to publish, reject to discard, or request revision if the tone or content needs adjustment.

### Check the Wiki

Agents write documentation as they work. Visit **WORK > Wiki** to see recent pages. Scribe handles most long-form content, with Quill polishing the details.

Wiki page types:
- **Spec** — Technical specifications and architecture docs
- **Runbook** — How-to guides and operational procedures
- **Release Notes** — Version and update announcements
- **Governance** — Policy and decision framework docs

### Monitor Social Performance

Check **OPS > Social Analytics** to see how your content is performing across platforms — follower growth, engagement rates, and recent post metrics.

---

## Weekly Rhythm

Beyond daily check-ins, here's what to look at weekly:

### Monday — Cost Review
Cipher produces a weekly cost report. Check **OPS > Costs** to review:
- Total API spend
- Cost per agent
- Budget vs. actual
- Any anomalies flagged by Cipher

### Tuesday — Content Pipeline
Echo produces weekly social drafts. Review and approve the batch in the Actions queue.

### Wednesday — Quality Check
Pixel runs accessibility scans. Check for any flagged issues in the task board or standup notes.

### Ongoing — Research Intel
Scout continuously monitors the market. Review research findings in the standup or check Scout's task comments for competitive intelligence.

---

## Using Quick Chat

Anytime you want to talk to an agent directly, click the **chat bubble** in the lower-right corner of any page.

1. Select an agent from the dropdown
2. Type your question or instruction
3. Get an immediate response

Examples:
- Ask **Nova**: *"What's the status on the marketing campaign?"*
- Ask **Cipher**: *"How much did we spend on API calls this week?"*
- Ask **Echo**: *"Draft a tweet about our new feature."*
- Ask **Scout**: *"What are our competitors doing with AI agents?"*

Quick Chat is great for ad-hoc questions. For larger directives, create a campaign or goal instead — that way agents work on it systematically across heartbeat cycles.

---

## Adjusting Autonomy

If things are running smoothly, let the system run in **Live mode** and check in once or twice a day.

If you want more control:
- Switch to **Safe mode** — agents propose but don't execute task changes
- **Pause specific projects** — freeze one initiative without stopping everything else
- **Lock mode** — full stop, for maintenance or major strategic shifts

Find these controls in **Config > Automation** or on the **Dashboard**.

---

## Common Scenarios

### "I want to launch a new product"
1. Create a campaign at **PLAN > Campaigns** with a clear title and description
2. Nova will break it into tasks and assign to relevant agents
3. Monitor progress on the task board
4. Approve marketing assets and social posts as they come through the queue

### "Costs are too high"
1. Check **OPS > Costs** for the breakdown
2. Ask Cipher via Quick Chat for optimization recommendations
3. Consider pausing non-essential campaigns
4. Review agent automation frequency in **Config > Automation**

### "I want agents to stop changing things"
1. Switch to **Safe mode** in Config > Automation
2. Agents will still observe and comment, but won't move tasks
3. Review agent proposals in the standup
4. Switch back to **Live mode** when you're ready

### "An agent did something I don't agree with"
1. Check the **Governance Log** in PLAN > Playbook to see what happened
2. Override or revert the action from the task board
3. Add a **seed memory** in Config > Memory to guide future behavior
4. All overrides are logged for transparency

### "I need research on a topic"
1. Ask Scout via Quick Chat for a quick answer
2. Or create a research task on the board and assign it to Scout
3. Scout will use live web search and deliver findings

---

## Summary

| When | What | Where |
|------|------|-------|
| Every morning | Check dashboard + clear approval queue | OPS > Dashboard, WORK > Actions |
| Every morning | Read standup summary | OPS > Standup |
| As needed | Create goals and campaigns | PLAN > Goals, PLAN > Campaigns |
| As needed | Review and manage tasks | WORK > Tasks |
| As needed | Approve social posts and content | WORK > Actions |
| Weekly (Mon) | Review costs | OPS > Costs |
| Weekly (Tue) | Review social drafts | WORK > Actions |
| Anytime | Talk to an agent | Quick Chat (lower-right) |
| When adjusting | Change execution mode | Config > Automation |

The system is designed so you can spend 10-15 minutes a day and stay fully in control. Agents handle the heavy lifting — you steer the ship.
